title: JudgeVerdict
description: A grader's output, carrying enough about the grader to be readable as evidence. The largest systematic evaluation to date — 21 judges, nine providers, ~541,000 judgments — found reliability and validity come apart: test-retest above 0.95 coexisted with severe position bias in two production-deployed judges. A verdict without its audit is a number of unknown meaning.

judge_id.description: Never the model under test. Self-grading is a cycle in the grading order, and a cycle does not merely risk reward hacking — it constructs it.

runs.description: Count of independent gradings. Single-run verdicts without variance present noise as a property of the system. Setting temperature to 0 does not make grading deterministic: borderline items still flip under forced greedy decoding, and newer frontier models have deprecated the parameter outright.

disagreement_rate.description: Fraction of runs disagreeing with the modal verdict. A first-class health metric, reported alongside the score rather than instead of it.

position_randomized.description: Whether candidate order was randomized. Position bias above 0.10 was measured in production-deployed judges whose test-retest reliability exceeded 0.95.

agreement.description: Chance-corrected agreement against a reference. Exact match is not admissible: it does not correct for chance and overstates discriminative ability by 33-41 percentage points against Cohen's kappa on the same data.

benchmark.description: Named, because judge rankings shift by up to 14 positions across benchmarks. Validation on one benchmark does not transfer to another.
